title: opacity versus a see-through background
summary: opacity fades the text too; a background colour with alpha fades only the background.
explanation: Both panels sit on the same gradient and both let it show through. The left one uses opacity: 0.6, which fades the whole element: background, border and the text inside.
The right one keeps opacity at 1 and gives the background colour an alpha channel instead: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6). Only the white fill is see-through; the text stays crisp.
Reach for an alpha colour when you want a frosted panel; use opacity when the whole thing should fade, such as a disabled button.
tryThis: Change opacity on .faded to 0.2: the text almost disappears.
Change the alpha in .tinted to 0.9, then to 0.2.
Give .faded's paragraph opacity: 1: it cannot become more opaque than its parent.

children.text: Only the white fill is see-through.
